phase: base lab environment; OIDC fixture running

steps.action: Configure single sign-on step 3 negative: Register provider with an issuer that cannot be reached
steps.actual: Register provider with an unreachable issuer showed "The change could not be saved. Try again." and no provider was stored.

steps.action: Configure single sign-on steps 1, 3 and 4: the operator's OIDC client (local fixture); Register provider; copy the displayed callback URL; registration turns on nothing; the secret is never returned
steps.expected: Saved; callback ends /api/auth/sso/callback on the instance address; SSO switches stay off but become available; Provider ID fixed
steps.actual: Register provider showed Saved and "Paste this callback URL into your IdP console: http://127.0.0.1:43310/api/auth/sso/callback". The instance address is BASE_URL http://127.0.0.1:43310. Both Single sign-on (SSO) switches stayed off and became available (["false","false"]). GET /api/v1/auth/sso-providers did not contain the client secret. After reload the Provider ID field was gone and the button read Save provider.

steps.action: Configure single sign-on steps 5 and 6: turn on SSO under Legal User Authentication; in a separate browser an invited staff account signs in through the identity provider
steps.expected: Callback succeeds; role Legal team member; the invited row becomes Active
steps.actual: The switch showed "Saved". In a separate browser, Continue with single sign-on went through the fixture's authorize endpoint and the OpenLaw callback to /, signed in as legal_team_member. The invited row now read Active with a role control (true).

steps.action: Matching an allowed email domain does not grant an uninvited person a staff role
steps.expected: No staff session and no staff account
steps.actual: With Business Portal SSO off and helix.example on the allowed list, doc030-auth-uninvited-p31639@helix.example ended on /auth/login?error=sso with me 401 and "Single sign-on failed. Try again.". Account created: none.

steps.action: Update a registered provider: Save provider with Client secret blank keeps it; a replacement rotates it; test a fresh sign-in after each
steps.expected: Saved both times; SSO works after each; the Client secret help tooltip
steps.actual: The Client secret help tooltip read "Leave blank to keep the current secret. Paste a new value to rotate.". Saving a Client ID change with a blank secret showed Saved; a fresh staff SSO sign-in worked (me 200). Saving a replacement secret showed Saved; another fresh sign-in worked (me 200).

steps.action: Update negative: an issuer that cannot be reached is refused and the previous provider configuration stays available
steps.expected: Refused; stored issuer unchanged; SSO still works
steps.actual: Save provider with an unreachable issuer showed "The change could not be saved. Try again.". The stored issuer stayed http://oidc:8080 and a fresh staff SSO sign-in still worked (me 200).

steps.action: Turn on SSO under Business Portal Authentication: an existing Business User signs in through the identity provider, and still can after its domain is removed; a new identity on the removed domain is refused
steps.expected: Portal before and after narrowing; newcomer refused with no account
steps.actual: doc030-auth-ssobu-p31639@helix.example entered the Portal through a sign-in link. The Business Portal SSO switch showed "Saved". Portal single sign-on for that Business User reached /portal/onboarding as business_user. After Remove helix.example (list ["northwind.example"]), the same identity still signed in through single sign-on (/portal/onboarding, business_user). A new identity on the removed domain ended on /portal/login?error=sso with "Single sign-on failed. Try again." and no account was created. helix.example was added back.

steps.action: Recover: with only SSO on under Legal, Administrator password sign-in still works; turn on Email and password and turn off SSO
steps.expected: Admin password sign-in works; Legal Team Member password sign-in works again; SSO off
steps.actual: With only Single sign-on (SSO) on for Legal users ({"password":false,"magicLink":false,"sso":true,"requireTwoFactor":false}), the staff page offered ["Continue with single sign-on","Administrator sign-in"] and Daniel still signed in with a password (me 200). Turning Email and password and Email magic link back on and SSO off in both cards gave {"legal":{"password":true,"magicLink":true,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false},"business":{"password":true,"magicLink":true,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false}}, and Nadia signed in with a password again (me 200).
